messages:
maria: heads-up — secret scanner flagged a GitHub App installation private key inside partner logs (partner-logs/2026-03-20/app-install-key.pem). possible plaintext exposure :rotating_light:

maria: scanner matched /-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----. Also saw a wrapped ciphertext label nearby: ci-kms-ciphertext=... but looks like the PEM is in the blob itself.

dmitri: ack. can you paste the blob path + id? i'll coordinate rotation + containment.

maria: blob path: gs://partner-logs/2026/03/20/app-install-key.pem (redacted). blob id: a1b2c3. found by secret-scanner at 12:13 UTC.

akash: if plaintext: immediate takedown. suggested runbook (short):
1) uninstall/revoke the GitHub App installation (prevent new tokens)
2) rotate GH App private key (generate new keypair, upload)
3) revoke any installation access tokens issued by that app
4) search+scrub partner logs and replace with redacted placeholder (preserve evidence read-only)
5) rotate any Vault roles/tokens that accepted that app as auth method
6) consider KMS rekey if wrapped blobs were mistakenly uploaded

dmitri: proposed owners: revoke app = @maria, rotate app key + update integrations = @dmitri, logs search/scrub = @sara, vault/kms rotation = @akash.

maria: i'm starting uninstall now. API snippet for uninstalling an installation via GH API:
```bash
# uninstall installation (example)
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: token $ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  "https://api.github.com/app/installations/INSTALLATION_ID"
```

dmitri: for key rotation i'll create a new RSA key and upload via the app settings/gh api. steps i will run:
```bash
openssl genrsa -out app_new.pem 2048
# convert if needed, then upload via GH API/console
gh api --method PATCH /app -f private_key="$(cat app_new.pem)"
```
Also will rotate any jwt-signed tokens and update CI creds pointing to the app.

sara: running a quick grep across partner logs to enumerate exposure. command i'm using:
```bash
gsutil ls gs://partner-logs/** | xargs -n1 gsutil cat | grep -n "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----"
```
Found 3 blobs: a1b2c3, d4e5f6, g7h8i9. replacing with redacted placeholder and preserving original copies to evidence bucket (read-only).

akash: vault/kms notes: if the partner uploaded a wrapped ciphertext that also contains plaintext (bad), do a vault rewrap only after we ensure original keypair is rotated. sample vault rewrap command:
```bash
# rewrap to rotate wrapping key/version
vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext="$CIPHERTEXT" -format=json > rewrapped.json
```
If using cloud KMS, create a new key version and re-encrypt data or disable old key version. also tighten transit policy so only the rotation service account can rewrap.

maria: @legal-bot heading for partner notification and incident intake. keeping low-bandwidth channel. will include list of affected partner blobs and timeline.

legal-bot: received. please include: affected orgs, risk assessment (tokens potentially minted), and remediation steps. legal will advise on disclosure.

dmitri: timeline proposal: 0-1h: uninstall/disable app and block integration; 1-3h: generate new app key + upload, revoke installation tokens; 3-6h: scrub partner logs (replace content, preserve evidence), run search for derived tokens; 6-24h: rotate Vault/KMS wrapping keys if any evidence indicates reuse, run audit.

akash: RBAC change: i'll push a temporary policy to restrict transit/rewrap to a designated rotation service account and remove broad service account bindings. will open a PR for vault-policy with TTL rollback.

sara: evidence preserved to gs://sec-evidence/4876543210/ (read-only). scrubbed originals replaced with redacted files containing: "REDACTED: potential private key, see sec-evidence bucket". updated lifecycle to reduce retention on partner logs.

maria: quick debugging Q: do we need to rotate any customer-facing keys? i think only the app key + any tokens issued by the installation. not rotating Vault root or KMS master unless evidence shows misuse.

dmitri: agreed. rotate app key and any installation tokens. if we see activity from the installation, expand scope. add scan rule to detect base64 PEM inside gz compressed logs (false negatives flagged).

maria: added checklist and will post final status here after each step. :white_check_mark:

sara: scrub done, evidence preserved, opening PR to ensure partner deletes local copies. notifying partner SRE.

dmitri: i'll schedule a postmortem in #postmortems and link the incident timeline. assigning follow-ups for infra + dev teams to update integrations.

maria: thanks team. continuing to monitor for suspicious API calls from the app installation and will update.
